title: Why he went to Europe: low pay in the States and a ten-day job
summary: He explains that salary cuts and no work at home made the $1,000-a-week offer attractive; he expected to be gone ten days while Buck was out of prison.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Why were you interested in expanding to Europe now, why didn't you just stay back in the states.
I just got through telling you they wanted to cut the salary, didn't I, from a thousand dollars. Didn't I?
after Nazarro, after the whole thing with Nazarro and now you were working for William Morris before you had left for Europe, you were working for William Morris with your salary $350 a week.
The reason for your going off to Europe.
are you on the way where you got there? Where did you get there? How can I make money in there, there ain't no theater, best I'd get is maybe $150 or $200 for the week.
So in the States you got a big cut in salary, so you started doing the tomato bit --
No, I didn't get no cut because I didn't work. That's the idea they were going to cut, but they didn't have work. But let me get you straight on that point will you? When I went to Germany

I went on the assumption that I wouldn't be gone but for 10 days. Buck is now out. He's not incarcerated now, he's out. Understand? I'm going to pick up a job, this job is worth a thousand dollars a week and all expenses paid. Now I done did the cafe thing already, understand? And Buck is out but I hadn't finished receiving mail for what I've done, received all the write-ups you get for the show. Here comes the mail concerning the show I was in, concerning me coming to Germany. So I can run over there for 10 days, I'll be right back. That's all I went for. So if I go over there, Buck and I won't have to start to work for no $600 or $300 a week over here. We'd come on over there. You understand? Now, that's my idea. But now look how long it's going to take me to get the fare to get him over here to Germany at $35 a show.
